subproblem.title: σ-finite Radon-Nikodym with a positive real density on a measurable carrier (Simon 6, proof of 8.1, (8))
subproblem.statement: Let X be a measurable space, let ν and μ be measures on X, and let B ⊆ X be a measurable set. Assume the restriction ν⌞B (A ↦ ν(A ∩ B)) is σ-finite, μ is σ-finite, μ(X ∖ B) = 0, and μ ≪ ν (ν(A) = 0 implies μ(A) = 0). Then there are a measurable set M ⊆ B and a measurable function θ : X → ℝ with the following properties: θ(x) > 0 for every x ∈ M; θ is ν-integrable on M ∩ K for every measurable K ⊆ X with μ(K) < ∞; and μ = (ν⌞M).withDensity(x ↦ ofReal θ(x)), i.e. μ(A) = ∫_{A∩M} θ dν for every measurable A ⊆ X.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (ν μ : Measure X) (B : Set X), MeasurableSet B → SigmaFinite (ν.restrict B) → SigmaFinite μ → μ Bᶜ = 0 → μ ≪ ν → ∃ (M : Set X) (θ : X → ℝ), M ⊆ B ∧ MeasurableSet M ∧ Measurable θ ∧ (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) ∧ (∀ K : Set X, MeasurableSet K → μ K < ∞ → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) ν) ∧ μ = (ν.restrict M).withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (θ x))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 8.1, display (8) (p. 174), in the form of steps 5-7 of the selected parent's proof. ν stands in for Hⁿ and B for the Borel carrier B₀. The integrability of step 7 is recorded for every measurable K of finite μ-measure. The Radon-Nikodym theorem is used in its abstract σ-finite form (the form recalled before Simon Ch. 1, 3.24).

Notation. For a measurable E ⊆ X, ν⌞E := ν.restrict E. It satisfies ν⌞E(A) = ν(A ∩ E) for every A ⊆ X (Measure.restrict_apply'). For a measure λ on X and any f : X → [0, ∞], λ.withDensity(f)(A) = ∫_A f dλ for every measurable A (withDensity_apply). For r ∈ ℝ with r ≥ 0, ‖r‖ₑ = ofReal(r) (Real.enorm_of_nonneg). 'λ-a.e.' means outside a λ-null set.

1. μ ≪ λ, where λ := ν⌞B. By Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.mk it suffices to treat measurable s with λ(s) = 0, i.e. ν(s ∩ B) = 0. Then μ(s ∩ B) = 0 because μ ≪ ν. Also μ(s ∖ B) ≤ μ(X ∖ B) = 0. Since s ⊆ (s ∩ B) ∪ (s ∖ B), we get μ(s) ≤ μ(s ∩ B) + μ(s ∖ B) = 0.

2. Radon-Nikodym. λ is σ-finite and μ is σ-finite, so the pair (μ, λ) has a Lebesgue decomposition (Mathlib instance Measure.haveLebesgueDecomposition_of_sigmaFinite). Let h := μ.rnDeriv λ : X → [0, ∞]; it is measurable (Measure.measurable_rnDeriv). The decomposition reads μ = μ.singularPart(λ) + λ.withDensity(h) (Measure.haveLebesgueDecomposition_add). Since μ ≪ λ, the singular part is 0 (Measure.singularPart_eq_zero_of_ac), so μ = λ.withDensity(h). This is Measure.withDensity_rnDeriv_eq. That lemma lives in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Decomposition/RadonNikodym.lean, which may be imported; the two lemmas above are already available after the frozen imports. Since μ is σ-finite, h(x) < ∞ for λ-a.e. x (Measure.rnDeriv_lt_top).

3. M and θ. Put M := B ∩ {x : 0 < h(x)} ∩ {x : h(x) < ∞} and θ(x) := (h(x)).toReal for x ∈ X. M is measurable because B and h are measurable (measurableSet_lt). Clearly M ⊆ B. θ is measurable (Measurable.ennreal_toReal) and θ ≥ 0 everywhere. For x ∈ M we have 0 < h(x) < ∞, so θ(x) > 0 (ENNReal.toReal_pos).

4. h = 1_M·g λ-a.e., where g(x) := ofReal(θ(x)) and 1_M·g is the indicator of M applied to g. λ-a.e. x satisfies both x ∈ B (ae_restrict_mem, since B is measurable) and h(x) < ∞ (step 2). Fix such an x. If h(x) > 0, then x ∈ M and g(x) = ofReal(h(x).toReal) = h(x), because h(x) ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). If h(x) = 0, then x ∉ M and both sides are 0.

5. The representation. By steps 2 and 4 and withDensity_congr_ae, μ = λ.withDensity(h) = λ.withDensity(1_M·g). Since M is measurable, λ.withDensity(1_M·g) = (λ⌞M).withDensity(g) (withDensity_indicator). Finally λ⌞M = (ν⌞B)⌞M = ν⌞(M ∩ B) (Measure.restrict_restrict), and M ∩ B = M because M ⊆ B. Hence μ = (ν⌞M).withDensity(x ↦ ofReal θ(x)).

6. Integrability. Let K ⊆ X be measurable with μ(K) < ∞. θ is measurable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for ν⌞(M ∩ K). Since θ ≥ 0, ‖θ(x)‖ₑ = g(x) for all x. Using (ν⌞M)⌞K = ν⌞(K ∩ M) = ν⌞(M ∩ K) (Measure.restrict_restrict), the formula of step 5 and withDensity_apply for the measurable K:
∫_{M∩K} ‖θ‖ₑ dν = ∫_K g d(ν⌞M) = (ν⌞M).withDensity(g)(K) = μ(K) < ∞.
So θ has a finite integral on M ∩ K. Together with measurability this is IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) ν. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ ≪ ν⌞B, from μ ≪ ν and μ(X ∖ B) = 0.
Lebesgue decomposition for the σ-finite pair (μ, ν⌞B) with zero singular part: μ = (ν⌞B).withDensity(h), h := μ.rnDeriv(ν⌞B) measurable, and h < ∞ (ν⌞B)-a.e. because μ is σ-finite.
M := B ∩ {0 < h < ∞} and θ := h.toReal: M and θ measurable, M ⊆ B, θ ≥ 0, θ > 0 on M.
h = 1_M·ofReal(θ) (ν⌞B)-a.e.; withDensity_indicator and restrict_restrict give μ = (ν⌞M).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ).
For measurable K with μ(K) < ∞: ∫_{M∩K} |θ| dν = μ(K) < ∞, so θ is ν-integrable on M ∩ K.

audit.reason: The proposition correctly assumes σ-finiteness of ν⌞B, without requiring global σ-finiteness of ν. Support and absolute continuity give μ ≪ ν⌞B. The measurable Radon–Nikodym derivative is finite almost everywhere; removing its zero and infinite values yields the required measurable carrier and strictly positive real density. The identity for the norm integral over M ∩ K gives exactly the claimed integrability. Every step is supplied, uses available hypotheses and is independent of the parent.

subproblem.title: Positive-upper-density subsets of a finite-measure open cover are Hⁿ-σ-finite, and ν-null ones are Hⁿ-null (Simon 6, proof of 8.1, (1) and (6))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let ν be a Borel measure on ℝ^P; for an arbitrary E ⊆ ℝ^P, ν(E) denotes its outer measure. Let (W_q)_{q∈ℕ} be open subsets of ℝ^P with ν(W_q) < ∞ for every q. Let S ⊆ ⋃_q W_q be an arbitrary, not necessarily measurable, set such that the upper density Θ*ⁿ(ν, x) = limsup_{r↓0} ν(B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) (dimensionalUpperDensity ν n univ x) is > 0 for every x ∈ S. Write Hⁿ = μHE[n] for the n-dimensional Hausdorff outer measure on ℝ^P. Then (i) there are sets C_i ⊆ ℝ^P (i ∈ ℕ) with S ⊆ ⋃_i C_i and Hⁿ(C_i) < ∞ for every i; and (ii) if ν(S) = 0, then Hⁿ(S) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Eucl P)) (W : ℕ → Set (Eucl P)) (S : Set (Eucl P)), (∀ q, IsOpen (W q)) → (∀ q, ν (W q) < ∞) → S ⊆ ⋃ q, W q → (∀ x ∈ S, 0 < dimensionalUpperDensity ν.toOuterMeasure (n : ℝ) univ x) → (∃ C : ℕ → Set (Eucl P), S ⊆ ⋃ i, C i ∧ ∀ i, (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) (C i) < ∞) ∧ (ν S = 0 → (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) S = 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 8.1 (pp. 173-174), display (1) and the step 'μ_T(P) = 0 and hence (6)'. These are steps 3 and 4 (second paragraph) of the selected parent's proof. Here they are stated for an arbitrary Borel measure ν in place of μ_T, and for an arbitrary countable open cover (W_q) of finite ν-measure in place of the exhaustion of U. The printed (1) bounds Hⁿ{x ∈ A : Θ*ⁿ > t} by t⁻¹μ_T(A). The comparison theorem used here (sibling density_comparison, Simon Ch. 1, 3.3) has an open set on its right-hand side. So the step from ν(S) = 0 to Hⁿ(S) = 0 goes through outer regularity of the finite measure ν⌞W_q (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15(1)), exactly as in step 4 of the parent proof.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P. It is evaluated on arbitrary sets and is monotone and countably subadditive. ν(E) for an arbitrary E ⊆ ℝ^P is the outer measure of ν. D(x) := Θ*ⁿ(ν, x) = dimensionalUpperDensity ν n univ x ∈ [0, ∞]. For an open (hence Borel) W, ν⌞W is the restricted measure (Mathlib ν.restrict W), with ν⌞W(O) = ν(O ∩ W) for every Borel O (Measure.restrict_apply) and ν⌞W(E) ≤ ν(E) for every E ⊆ ℝ^P (Measure.restrict_apply_le, or Measure.le_iff'.1 Measure.restrict_le_self E). All arithmetic is in [0, ∞].

Tool (sibling density_comparison). For every set A ⊆ ℝ^P, every open V ⊇ A and every t ∈ [0, ∞] with t ≤ D(x) for all x ∈ A: t·Hⁿ(A) ≤ ν(V).

1. Pieces. For j, q ∈ ℕ let t_j := (j+1)⁻¹ ∈ (0, 1] and A_{j,q} := {x : x ∈ S, x ∈ W_q, t_j ≤ D(x)}. Then A_{j,q} ⊆ S and A_{j,q} ⊆ W_q, and t_j ≤ D(x) for all x ∈ A_{j,q}. Also t_j ≠ 0, because j + 1 ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.inv_ne_zero).

2. The pieces cover S: S ⊆ ⋃_j ⋃_q A_{j,q}. Let x ∈ S. Since S ⊆ ⋃_q W_q, there is q with x ∈ W_q. Since D(x) > 0, i.e. D(x) ≠ 0, there is k ∈ ℕ with k⁻¹ < D(x) (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt; here 0⁻¹ = ∞). As k ≤ k + 1, t_k = (k+1)⁻¹ ≤ k⁻¹ < D(x) (ENNReal.inv_le_inv). Hence x ∈ A_{k,q}.

3. Proof of (i). Fix j, q. W_q is open and contains A_{j,q}, and t_j ≤ D on A_{j,q}. The tool with A := A_{j,q}, V := W_q and t := t_j gives t_j·Hⁿ(A_{j,q}) ≤ ν(W_q) < ∞. If Hⁿ(A_{j,q}) were ∞, then t_j·Hⁿ(A_{j,q}) = ∞ because t_j ≠ 0, a contradiction. Hence Hⁿ(A_{j,q}) < ∞ (ENNReal.mul_lt_top_iff). Now index the pieces by one natural number. Let Nat.pair : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ be Mathlib's pairing function (Mathlib/Data/Nat/Pairing.lean) and Nat.unpair : ℕ → ℕ × ℕ its inverse, so Nat.unpair (Nat.pair j q) = (j, q) (Nat.unpair_pair). Put C_i := A_{(Nat.unpair i).1, (Nat.unpair i).2} for i ∈ ℕ. Then Hⁿ(C_i) < ∞ for every i. If x ∈ S, step 2 gives j, q with x ∈ A_{j,q} = C_{Nat.pair j q}. Hence S ⊆ ⋃_i C_i, which proves (i).

4. Proof of (ii), one piece. Assume ν(S) = 0 and fix j, q. We show Hⁿ(A_{j,q}) = 0. Suppose not. Then c := t_j·Hⁿ(A_{j,q}) > 0, a product of two nonzero elements of [0, ∞] (ENNReal.mul_pos). The measure ν⌞W_q has total mass ν(W_q) < ∞, so it is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P (isFiniteMeasure_restrict). A finite Borel measure on a (pseudo)metrizable space is weakly regular, hence outer regular. In Mathlib these are the instances Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure and Measure.OuterRegular, found automatically once IsFiniteMeasure (ν.restrict (W q)) is in context; compare Simon Ch. 1, 1.15(1). We have ν⌞W_q(S) ≤ ν(S) = 0 < c. Outer regularity, applied to the arbitrary set S (Mathlib Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt), gives an open O ⊇ S with ν⌞W_q(O) < c. As O is Borel, this says ν(O ∩ W_q) < c. The set V := O ∩ W_q is open and contains A_{j,q}, because A_{j,q} ⊆ S ⊆ O and A_{j,q} ⊆ W_q. The tool with A := A_{j,q}, this V and t := t_j gives c = t_j·Hⁿ(A_{j,q}) ≤ ν(V) < c, a contradiction. Hence Hⁿ(A_{j,q}) = 0.

5. Proof of (ii), conclusion. By step 4, Hⁿ(⋃_q A_{j,q}) = 0 for every j and then Hⁿ(⋃_j ⋃_q A_{j,q}) = 0, by countable subadditivity (measure_iUnion_null twice). By step 2, S ⊆ ⋃_j ⋃_q A_{j,q}, so Hⁿ(S) = 0 by monotonicity (measure_mono_null). This proves (ii). ∎
proof_key_steps: Pieces A_{j,q} := {x ∈ S ∩ W_q : (j+1)⁻¹ ≤ Θ*ⁿ(ν, x)} cover S, since Θ*ⁿ(ν, x) > 0 exceeds some (k+1)⁻¹ (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt).
density_comparison with V := W_q gives (j+1)⁻¹·Hⁿ(A_{j,q}) ≤ ν(W_q) < ∞, so Hⁿ(A_{j,q}) < ∞; reindexing by Nat.unpair gives the cover C_i.
If ν(S) = 0: ν⌞W_q is finite, hence outer regular, so some open O ⊇ S has ν(O ∩ W_q) < (j+1)⁻¹·Hⁿ(A_{j,q}). density_comparison with V := O ∩ W_q is then contradictory unless Hⁿ(A_{j,q}) = 0.
Countable subadditivity and monotonicity give Hⁿ(S) = 0.

audit.reason: All hypotheses and both conclusions match the standalone Lean proposition. The reciprocal-density pieces cover S and have finite Hausdorff measure by density comparison. For null transfer, outer regularity is correctly applied to the finite Borel measure ν⌞W_q, including for nonmeasurable S; comparison then forces every piece to be Hausdorff-null. Countable subadditivity completes the proof. Its sole dependency is correctly directed to density_comparison.
